summary: Exact integer checks confirm the bound forty residual members and the two auxiliary bounds of four used in Profile A. A deliberate relaxation shows why the inherited at-most-two-high-points theorem matters: replacing residual caps fourteen/nine by fifteen/ten permits forty-five in the scalar model. The manuscript uses the stronger justified caps and does not mistake scalar feasibility for actual-family realizability.

checks.scope: Integer margins and robustness of the two-star incidence bound
checks.method: Independently enumerate q=0,...,12 and m=0,...,61 satisfying 2m≤9q and 3m≤14(12−q)+9q; repeat with degree caps fifteen and ten. Retain executable arithmetic in scratch/beta/round05_bounds.py.
checks.observation: The exact caps allow maximum m=40, only at q=9. Directly, m=41 would force q≥10 from overlap incidence and q≤9 from U incidence. Relaxed caps permit m=45,q=9, confirming that the proof needs the inherited high-point restriction to obtain the residual degree cap fourteen rather than fifteen. This is an auxiliary scalar calculation; it asserts no family with m=40 or m=45 exists.

checks.scope: Small auxiliary combinatorial caps in Profile A
checks.method: Enumerate all subfamilies of the five edges of C5 for pairwise intersection, and all sixty-four graphs on four labeled vertices for the actual three-edge sunflower predicate; compare with Sections 4.2 and 4.3.
checks.observation: An intersecting C5 edge family has at most two edges, so the two coordinate projections allow at most four distinct completions. A three-sunflower-free graph on four vertices has at most four edges; exactly three labeled maximal four-edge families occur, each a four-cycle. Thus the separate completion and outsider-fiber bounds are exact for their auxiliary graph hypotheses. These checks corroborate the prose argument without claiming a new formal proof.
